name: Genaya API
description:
# Genaya API

The Genaya REST API lets you build on top of your Genaya organization:
read and write appointments, clients, contacts, invoices, estimates,
expenses, lead tables and rows, tasks, task environments, reminders,
campaign audiences (push your signups straight into a marketing audience)
and the data tables of the websites Genaya built for you (the leads and
bookings a site collects, plus any custom table), plus read-only access
to your team roster. Outbound webhooks push events to your server as
they happen - see Webhooks below.

The API is available on the **Individual plan and above** (the free trial
gets test keys only and 500 requests in total). Every plan includes a pool
of requests each billing period - see "Rate limits" and "Plans and
pricing" below. Everything is scoped to your organization by the API key
you use - you can never see or touch another organization's data.

Base URL:

```
https://api.genaya.com/v1
```

## Getting started

1. In the Genaya app, open **Settings > Developer** and create an API key.
   The full key is shown once at creation - store it securely.
2. Send the key as a bearer token on every request:

```bash
curl https://api.genaya.com/v1/appointments \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer gny_live_your_key_here"
```

## Authentication

Authenticate with a Genaya-issued API key in the `Authorization` header:

```
Authorization: Bearer gny_live_xxx
```

Keys come in two modes:

- `gny_live_...` - production traffic.
- `gny_test_...` - operates on the **same** organization data but is flagged
  so you can separate test traffic. There is no isolated sandbox dataset.

A missing, malformed, or revoked key returns `401 authentication_error`. A
key whose organization is on a plan without API access returns `403
permission_error` with code `plan_required` (the API needs the Individual
plan or above). On a free trial only test keys exist: a live key returns
`403 permission_error` with code `live_key_requires_paid_plan`, and a test
key on any write returns `403 permission_error` with code
`test_mode_read_only`. An organization that switched the Developer API off
under Settings > Features returns `403 permission_error` with code
`feature_disabled`.

API keys are server-to-server credentials. Do not embed them in browser or
mobile apps.

## Scopes

Each key carries optional per-resource scopes, for example
`appointments:read` or `invoices:write`. A key with **no scopes** has full
access (forward-compatible default). When scopes are present, a request that
needs a scope the key lacks returns `403 permission_error` with code
`insufficient_scope`. Each endpoint documents the scope it requires.

## Errors

Errors use a consistent envelope:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "invalid_request_error",
    "code": "missing_field",
    "message": "clientName is required.",
    "param": "clientName"
  }
}
```

| HTTP | type | Meaning |
|------|------|---------|
| 400 | `invalid_request_error` | Malformed or missing parameters |
| 401 | `authentication_error` | Bad, missing, or revoked key |
| 402 | `usage_limit_error` | The prepaid balance has nothing left for API requests past the included pool, or the trial's 500 requests are used up (see the message) |
| 403 | `permission_error` | Key lacks the scope, the plan has no API access, a live key on a trial, or the feature is switched off |
| 404 | `not_found` | No such resource in this organization |
| 409 | `idempotency_error` | Idempotency-Key reused with a different body |
| 422 | `validation_error` | Well-formed but rejected by a business rule |
| 429 | `rate_limit_error` | Rate limited (see Retry-After) |
| 500 | `api_error` | Unexpected server error |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | A counter the request depends on could not be read (see Retry-After) - today only the Genaya AI credits pool on `POST /v1/ai/ask` |

## Success envelope

- Single object: `{ "data": { ... } }`
- List: `{ "object": "list", "data": [ ... ], "has_more": true, "next_cursor": "<id>" }`

Every resource object includes `id`, `object`, `createdAt`, and `updatedAt`
(ISO-8601 strings). Fields are canonical camelCase.

## Pagination

Lists are cursor-based. Pass `limit` (default 25, max 100) and
`starting_after=<resourceId>` to page forward. The response includes
`has_more` and `next_cursor`; keep requesting with
`starting_after=next_cursor` until `has_more` is `false`. Lists are returned
in a stable order; sort client-side on `createdAt` if you need chronological
order.

## Filtering by created date

Every list endpoint accepts optional `from` and `to` query parameters that
filter by the resource's **created date**. Pass an ISO-8601 date
(`2026-06-01`) or full timestamp (`2026-06-01T00:00:00Z`). A bare date for
`from` snaps to the start of that UTC day and `to` to the end, so
`?from=2026-06-01&to=2026-06-30` returns everything created in June. When a
date window is applied, results are ordered newest-first by created date.
(The team roster endpoint has no date window.)

## Polling for changes

The main list endpoints (appointments, clients, contacts, invoices,
estimates, expenses, tasks, reminders, and leads) also accept
`updated_since` - an ISO-8601 date or timestamp that returns only records
updated on or after that time, ordered by `updatedAt` **ascending** so a
poller pages forward and resumes its next poll from the newest
`updatedAt` it has seen. It is mutually exclusive with the `from`/`to`
created-date window (and with any schedule window) - combining them
returns 400. Records that have never been written since change tracking
shipped have no `updatedAt` yet and are absent from this window until
something touches them; for a full sync, walk the plain list first and
use `updated_since` for incremental polls after that. For push instead of
poll, use Webhooks below.

## Idempotency

Safely retry create requests by sending an `Idempotency-Key` header (any
unique string). Genaya stores the first response for 24 hours and replays it
on a retry with the same key. Reusing a key with a different request body
returns `409 idempotency_error`.

## Rate limits

Limits scale with the organization's plan. A "request" is a weighted
unit - see "How requests are counted" below.

| Plan | Per minute, per key | Per minute, per organization | Per day, per organization | Writes per day, per organization |
|------|---------------------|------------------------------|---------------------------|----------------------------------|
| Free trial | 10 | 20 | 500 (total for the trial) | 0 (test keys cannot write) |
| Individual | 30 | 60 | 10,000 | 2,000 |
| Pro | 100 | 200 | 50,000 | 20,000 |
| Business | 300 | 600 | 250,000 | 100,000 |
| Enterprise | 600 | 1,200 | 1,000,000 | unlimited |

The per-organization ceilings apply across every key the organization
holds, so ten keys do not mean ten times the budget. The per-day column
is a database-protection ceiling and is separate from the monthly request
pool under "Plans and pricing": a Business organization can spend its
500,000 pool requests over a month but never more than 250,000 of them in
one day.

Heavy requests - `POST /v1/ai/ask` and a commission report rendered as
PNG - also share a per-key sub-window of 20% of the per-minute limit in
weighted units, never below 10 (one AI question a minute on every plan):
free trial 10, Individual 10, Pro 20, Business 60, Enterprise 120. That
keeps one expensive loop from starving the cheap calls next to it. Lists
are never in that window; a larger page simply weighs more.

Every response carries the current state of every window:

- `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` - the
  per-minute window for this key (reset is epoch seconds).
- `X-RateLimit-Limit-Org` - the per-minute ceiling for the whole
  organization.
- `X-RateLimit-Limit-Day`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining-Day`,
  `X-RateLimit-Reset-Day` - the per-day window for the organization.
- `X-Write-Quota-Limit`, `X-Write-Quota-Remaining`, `X-Write-Quota-Reset` -
  on writes (POST, PATCH, PUT, DELETE): the organization's daily write
  quota. Reads never count against it.
- `X-Api-Requests-Used`, `X-Api-Requests-Included` - the organization's
  request pool for the current billing period (see "Plans and pricing").

When you exceed a window you get `429 rate_limit_error` with a
`Retry-After` header (seconds). Back off and retry after the window
resets. `GET /v1/usage` returns every window and the pool in one call.

## How requests are counted

Every request is weighted so that expensive calls pay for what they cost:

| Request | Weight |
|---------|--------|
| Read, create, update or delete a single record | 1 |
| A list | 1 + 1 per 25 records requested (`limit` 25 = 2, 50 = 3, 100 = 5) |
| `POST /v1/ai/ask` | 10 (the AI answer itself is 10 Genaya AI credits, like a question in the app - a separate meter) |
| A commission report as PNG (`format=png`) | 5 |
| `/ping`, `/account`, `/usage` | 1 |

Weights apply to the rate-limit windows and to the request pool alike. A
request that fails with a 5xx is never counted, and neither is a request
refused by a limit (429) or by the usage gate (402). A retry that replays
a stored `Idempotency-Key` response is a normal request: it passes the
limiter and counts its full weight, so a retry loop still spends the pool.

Through the MCP connector (`POST /v1/mcp`) the JSON-RPC request itself
counts 1 on the rate-limit windows only - it is never billed to the pool -
and every `tools/call` inside it counts the weight of the REST request it
makes, on the windows and on the pool, exactly as a direct call would. A
tool call refused by a limit or by the write quota returns the standard
error envelope as the tool's error text; a 402 or 429 on the outer
`POST /v1/mcp` itself comes back as the REST error envelope, not as a
JSON-RPC error. A JSON-RPC batch may carry at most 20 messages.

## Plans and pricing

Every plan includes a pool of weighted requests per billing period:

| Plan | Included requests per billing period | API keys |
|------|--------------------------------------|----------|
| Free trial | 500 in total (test keys only, read-only) | 1 |
| Individual | 10,000 | 2 |
| Pro | 50,000 | 5 |
| Business | 500,000 | 20 |
| Enterprise | unlimited | unlimited |

Past the included pool, extra requests cost **$1.00 per 10,000** (charged
in 1,000-request steps, $0.10 each) from the organization's prepaid
balance under Settings > Billing - the same balance that pays for extra
texts, calls, video and extra Genaya AI credits. API requests are a
separate meter from Genaya AI credits: a `POST /v1/ai/ask` answer is 10
Genaya AI credits (like a question in the app) on top of its request
weight. The organization's billing contacts get a heads-up at 80% of the
pool and again at 100%. While the pool has allowance left, requests are
always served, even when the prepaid balance is empty. Once the pool is
used and the prepaid balance is empty (and Auto-pay is off), the API
answers `402 usage_limit_error` with code `out_of_usage_credit` and a
plain message; nothing is dropped silently. A free trial that has used
its 500 requests answers `402 usage_limit_error` with code
`trial_request_limit`. Limits and the pool apply within a few seconds of
a change, so a request sent right after the balance runs out can still
succeed.

`GET /v1/usage` reports the pool (`requests.used`, `requests.included`,
`requests.remaining`, `requests.resetsAt`) and the key count next to the
rate-limit windows.

## Versioning

The API is versioned in the path (`/v1`). Breaking changes ship as a new
version (`/v2`); `/v1` is a stable, frozen contract.

## Webhooks

Genaya can push events to your server the moment they happen instead of
you polling for changes. Create endpoints in the app under **Settings >
Developer > Webhooks**, or programmatically via `POST
/v1/webhook-endpoints` (the REST-hook pattern integration platforms
use). Every delivery is an HTTPS POST carrying a JSON event envelope:

```json
{
  "id": "evt_8ZwQ3kX9pL2mN0aB",
  "object": "event",
  "type": "invoice.paid",
  "created": "2026-08-03T17:24:05.000Z",
  "organization_id": "9f2kX0aBcDeFgHiJ",
  "data": { "object": { "object": "invoice", "id": "..." } }
}
```

Delivery is **at-least-once** - dedupe on the event `id`. Respond with a
2xx within 10 seconds; anything else (including a redirect) counts as a
failure and is retried with backoff (1m, 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h, 24h - 7 total
attempts) before the delivery is marked dead, and an endpoint whose
deliveries keep going dead is automatically paused. Every request is
signed: the `X-Genaya-Signature` header is `t=<unix>,v1=<hex>`, where
`v1` is the HMAC-SHA256 of `<t>.<raw body>` keyed with the endpoint's
secret - verify with a timing-safe compare and reject stale timestamps.
The full secret is returned only in the create response and masked
afterward. See the Webhooks endpoints for the event catalog
(`GET /v1/webhook-endpoints/events`) and management operations.

## MCP (Genaya Connect)

Genaya is also an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, so ChatGPT, Claude,
Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code and your own agents can use Genaya as a
signed-in team member: one endpoint at `https://api.genaya.com/mcp`,
"Sign in with Genaya" (OAuth 2.1 with PKCE, discovery at
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` and
`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`), and tools that run the same
Genaya AI brain the app uses, as that member, in the organization they
picked. This release ships `whoami` and `ask_genaya` (read-only); actions
and typed lookups follow. API keys with a per-key "Allow MCP" switch on
the same endpoint are coming - until then the API-key MCP server stays at
`POST /v1/mcp`. See the "MCP" and "Sign in with Genaya" sections.

## Coming soon

Official SDKs are not part of v1 yet - the API is plain HTTPS + JSON and
works with any HTTP client.
